title: Logic Pro 12 Update
intro: Logic Pro 12 arrived on 28 January 2026. It runs only on Macs with Apple silicon and needs macOS Sequoia 15.6 or later. The headline additions are the Synth Player and Chord ID. This section covers what is new, plus an upgrade playbook for any major release.

notice.title: One requirement before anything else
notice.text: Logic Pro 12 requires an Apple silicon Mac running macOS 15.6 or later. There is no Intel version. If you are still on an Intel machine, Logic Pro 11 is the end of the road — plan around that before you update anything.

src.label: Production Expert — Logic Pro 12: AI features, new tools and Intel Mac support dropped

tips.t: Synth Player lives inside Bass Player and Keyboard Player
tips.d: Synth Player is not a new Session Player. It is a set of styles inside the Bass Player and Keyboard Player you already have. Create a Bass Player or Keyboard Player track, open the Session Player Editor and choose a Synth style. Both players can follow the Chord track, so one progression drives bass and keys together.

src.label: Apple — Intro to Synth Player styles in Logic Pro for Mac
Apple — Chords and Session Players in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: Pick the Synth Keyboard style before you touch anything else
tips.d: The Synth Keyboard Player has three styles: Rhythmic Chords, Modulated Pad and Simple Pad. Audition all three against the same chords before you start editing.

src.label: Apple — Intro to Synth Player styles in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: Synth Bass ships with three distinct characters
tips.d: The Synth Bass Player has three styles: 808 Bass, Pump Bass and Sequenced Bass. Audition all three before you start editing the pattern.

src.label: Apple — Intro to Synth Player styles in Logic Pro for Mac
Apple — Logic Pro for Mac release notes

tips.t: Shape the Pump Bass pump directly
tips.d: Pump Bass gets its pumping from modulated ducking, like a sidechained compressor, and you can shape it. In the Session Player Editor, click the Details button. Drag the Amount knob vertically to set how hard it ducks, and the Shape knob to change the ducking curve.

src.label: Apple — Edit a Synth Bass Player performance in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: Point Synth Player at a third-party synth
tips.d: The performance and the sound source are separate. A Synth Player style loads an Alchemy patch by default, but you can use Synth Players with any software instrument plug-in or an external MIDI tone generator. You keep the chord-following performance and choose your own sound.

src.label: Apple — Intro to Synth Player styles in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: Chord ID reads chords off audio, not just MIDI
tips.d: Drag a guitar demo, a piano take or a rough bounce onto the Chord track. Chord ID analyses the region and adds the chords it finds to the Chord track as a chord group. It works on audio and MIDI regions, and Apple says it handles single instruments and full mixes.

src.label: Apple — Analyze the chords in audio or MIDI regions in Logic Pro for Mac
Apple — Logic Pro for Mac release notes

tips.t: Check Chord ID's chords before you build on them
tips.d: Chord ID writes what it finds straight onto the Chord track as a chord group. Play it back against the source before you build on it. If a chord is wrong, edit it on the Chord track: you can change the root note and chord type, add or remove extensions, and set a bass note other than the root.

src.label: Apple — Analyze the chords in audio or MIDI regions in Logic Pro for Mac
Apple — Edit chords in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: Everything downstream follows the Chord track
tips.d: Once Chord ID has populated the Chord track, other tracks can lock to it. Apple: "By following the Chord track, multiple tracks — such as tracks using Step Sequencer, Session Player tracks, and other software instrument tracks — can play in sync harmonically." Set a Session Player region to follow with Control-click > Chords > Follow Global Chord Track; set a Step Sequencer pattern to follow by choosing Chord Track, which renames the note rows to chord degrees. One analysis pass can arrange several parts at once.

tips.t: Run Chord ID on your own old bounces
tips.d: Lost the project but kept the bounce? Drag the bounce onto the Chord track and Chord ID adds its chords there as a chord group. Check them against the bounce, fix any that are wrong, then rebuild from there.

tips.t: Preview sound packs before you download them
tips.d: Open Logic Pro > Sound Library and click a sound pack to preview it before you commit to downloading. It is also where you reclaim space: click Manage Packs, then click Delete next to a pack you no longer need. The total space all installed packs use is shown at the top of the list, and each pack's size appears in the list.

src.label: Apple — Download additional sound packs in Logic Pro for Mac
Apple — Logic Pro for Mac release notes

tips.t: Reanalyze and try each Character
tips.d: When the mix changes, click Reanalyze in Mastering Assistant so it analyses the project again. Then try the Character options: Transparent (the default), Clean, Valve and Punch. A/B each against the master you signed off on before you call it finished. Transparent, Punch and Valve require an Apple silicon Mac.

src.label: Apple — Mastering Assistant parameters in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: Logic Pro 12 drops Intel Macs entirely
tips.d: It requires a Mac with Apple silicon and macOS 15.6 or later. If you are on an Intel Mac, you can't run it, so check your machine before you plan an upgrade.

src.label: Apple — Logic Pro for Mac - Technical Specifications
Apple Support — Logic Pro - Tech Specs

tips.t: Never update in the middle of a paid project
tips.d: The one rule that matters. Finish and deliver, then update. A new version halfway through a mix is a self‑inflicted deadline problem.

tips.t: Back up the current version before you update
tips.d: Use Apple's procedure. Make a folder in Applications named for the version (for example "Logic Pro 11.1.2"), select Logic Pro and choose File > Compress "Logic Pro", then move Logic Pro.zip into that folder. If the update causes problems, reinstall the backed-up version.

src.label: Apple Support — Back up Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: Back up your key commands and channel strip settings
tips.d: Choose Logic Pro > Key Commands > Edit, click the Actions button, choose Save As, name your set and save it somewhere safe, such as an external drive. Your channel strip settings live in ~/Music/Audio Music Apps/Channel Strip Settings, so copy that folder too.

src.label: Apple Support — Create custom keyboard shortcuts for Logic Pro for Mac
Logic Studio Training Wiki — Channel strip settings
macProVideo — Demystifying Logic Pro X's Plug-In Settings, Channel Strip Settings & Patches

tips.t: Consolidate and archive your three most important projects
tips.d: File > Project Management > Consolidate on each, then copy them to a separate drive. If the new version changes something, you have untouched originals.

src.label: Apple Support — Consolidate assets in a Logic Pro for Mac project

tips.t: Check your critical third‑party plugins against the new version first
tips.d: Plugin developers lag major DAW releases. Check their compatibility pages before you update, not after.

tips.t: Note your current I/O and buffer settings
tips.d: Screenshot your Audio settings before you update — output device, input device and I/O buffer size. It takes five seconds, and if anything about your setup looks different afterwards you can restore the exact configuration you were working with instead of guessing at it.

src.label: Apple Support — Avoid system overloads in Logic Pro for Mac
macProVideo — Logic Pro X Audio Preferences Explained

tips.t: Update macOS and Logic separately, a week apart
tips.d: If something breaks, you want to know which of the two did it.

tips.t: Read the new Key Commands list for additions
tips.d: After every update, choose Logic Pro > Key Commands > Edit and browse for commands you haven't seen before. Click Unused to show commands that have no shortcut yet. For any you'll use, select it, click Learn by Key Label and press the keys you want.

src.label: Apple Support — Create custom keyboard shortcuts for Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: Test your bounce path end to end before you need it
tips.d: Bounce a short section to every format you deliver in. Export bugs are the ones that bite at the worst possible moment.

tips.t: Give yourself a deliberate hour to explore
tips.d: Not on a project. Open a scratch session and use every new feature once. An hour of play beats a month of accidental discovery.
